findings.title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted
findings.body: TagDevice now propagates the device-limit error to authentication, but tagDeviceUI still inserts the device ID into its 29-minute local cache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When a new device is rejected because the limit is full, that cache entry remains. A second request with the same device ID hits the cache, returns nil without checking the store, and authenticates successfully. Concurrent requests can likewise use the entry before the first admission check finishes. Cache only successful admissions and ensure requests cannot treat an in-progress admission as successful; add a test that retries a rejected device.

findings.title: Device count and admission are not atomic
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts active devices in one database session and inserts the new device in a separate session without any serialization. When the count is one below the configured limit, multiple requests with distinct device IDs can all observe the available slot and each insert successfully, exceeding the limit. This also occurs across Grafana replicas sharing the database, so a process-local lock alone would not fix it. Serialize the count-and-admission operation at the database level and test simultaneous admissions at the limit.
